caption_v6: \caption{\textbf{In the linear autoencoder, gradient descent without a regularizer stays unreliable at every sample size on the criteria that see the gauge (a--c), whereas weight decay, tied weights, and small initialization are reliable on all four from $N=2^{12}$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:gauge}).} (a--d) Fraction of disjoint run pairs, differing in initialization and training sample, within the preregistered tolerance against the sample size $N$ ($N=\infty$ is the population). Bars are one-sided $95\%$ Clopper--Pearson bounds; grey lines are the decision levels stated in (d). Panels (a--c) test parts~1 to~3; the projector (d) does not see the gauge (part~4) and is the control. (e) Anisotropy of the learned gauge at $N=\infty$, measured and as predicted by the theorem part in the row label: median and 10th to 90th percentile of runs. Weight decay, tied weights, and small initialization use the preregistered step: part~3 holds at any step, and small initialization keeps the imbalance $C$ of part~1 near zero, which the rules outside the theorem change. Table~\ref{tab:app-s13a} gives every decision; Figure~\ref{fig:exp-gauge-case} repeats (b), (d), and (e).}
